correctness.rationale: An explicitly specified 6,561-state finite automaton encodes every Roman labeling of every \(P(n,2)\) for \(n\ge7\). A 6,561-entry integer potential is checked against every one of its 48,681 arcs, giving nonnegative reduced cost equal to \(7w(f)-8n\) on closed walks. An independent SCC traversal proves all tight closed walks are repetitions of a single directed seven-cycle and explicitly recovers the given primitive word. Repeating this word attains weight \(8m\). Therefore exactly its seven rotations are optimal for all \(m\ge1\). Independent support enumeration verifies seven minima at \(n=7,14\). Pairwise two-label support intersections yield the sharp \(2m\) exchange threshold and cycle/complete graph regimes. The finite verification is a proof certificate applying to infinitely many lengths, not a finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The classical optimal-weight formula leaves open the natural structure of optimizers in a periodic graph family. The complete classification rules out arbitrary phase defects across an unbounded number of seven-column blocks: exactly seven optimizers survive, a nontrivial rigidity phenomenon. The support-exchange threshold grows sharply as \(2m\), making this exact infinite-family benchmark relevant to reconfiguration and robustness of minimal Roman placements. This is a motivated structural classification, not a routine recomputation of the known minimum weight.
